description.summary: touchpad gesture and pointer axis bindings

protocol.description:
This fork-only protocol (newm-river, a fork of river) lets the river-window-management-v1 window manager bind touchpad gestures (swipe, pinch, hold) and pointer axis motion (wheel, two-finger scroll) with a modifier mask, the way river_pointer_binding_v1 binds buttons.
A gesture that begins with the finger count and the exact modifiers of an enabled binding is consumed: the window manager receives begin, update and end events and no client receives the gesture over pointer-gestures-v1. A gesture that matches no enabled binding reaches clients as before. Likewise an axis event whose orientation and modifiers match an enabled axis binding is consumed and reported to the window manager instead of the client under the pointer. Since version 4 the seat object also reports the pointer's motion with and without acceleration (pointer_motion), which river-window-management-v1 does not.
Events are sent as part of a manage sequence, before river_window_manager_v1.manage_start, like river_pointer_binding_v1 pressed and released. Motion between two manage sequences is coalesced into a single update, axis or pointer_motion event.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in IETF RFC 2119.

interface.name: newm_river_gestures_v1
interface.description: This global interface should only be advertised to the client if the river_window_manager_v1 global is also advertised.

entry.name: object_already_created
entry.summary: newm_river_gestures_seat_v1 already created for the seat

request.name: destroy
request.description: Objects created from this one are not affected.

request.name: get_seat

description.summary: get the gesture bindings of a seat

request.description: It is a protocol error to make this request more than once for a seat. If the river_seat_v1 is inert the new object is inert too.

interface.name: newm_river_gestures_seat_v1
interface.description: Destroying this object destroys the bindings created from it: they turn inert.

request.name: get_gesture_binding
request.description: Bind gestures of the given kind that begin with exactly finger_count fingers while exactly the given modifiers are held. The binding starts disabled. If several enabled bindings match, the oldest wins.

event.name: desktop_press

description.summary: a pointer button pressed on the desktop

event.description: A pointer button no pointer binding takes was pressed where neither a window nor a shell surface is: over no surface, or over a layer surface of the background or bottom layer (a wallpaper). The press still reaches that layer surface. x and y are the pointer's position in the compositor's logical coordinate space. With no window there the window manager learns of the press only from this event, for example to make that output the active one. Sent as it happens, outside manage sequences.

event.name: pointer_motion

description.summary: relative pointer motion, with and without acceleration

event.description:
The relative motion of the seat's pointer summed since the previous pointer_motion event, twice: dx and dy as the cursor moves (with the pointer acceleration libinput applies), unaccel_dx and unaccel_dy without it, as wp_relative_pointer_v1 reports them. Absolute motion counts as its displacement in both. Motion a pointer constraint holds back is not counted; motion the output edges clamp away is, as in river_seat_v1.op_delta. Warps do not count.
Sent as part of a manage sequence, before river_window_manager_v1.manage_start, if the pointer moved since the previous pointer_motion event, whether or not a pointer operation runs. Motion before this object was created is not reported.
river_seat_v1.op_delta and pointer_position carry the accelerated motion only. With this event the window manager can follow the hand instead, for example in a modifier key pan that takes only a share s of the acceleration: unaccel + s * (accelerated - unaccel) per event, which is linear, so the same expression of these sums.

request.name: get_axis_binding
request.description: Bind axis events of the given orientation (wheel or touchpad scroll) while exactly the given modifiers are held. The binding starts disabled. If several enabled bindings match, the oldest wins.

interface.name: newm_river_gesture_binding_v1
interface.description: enable and disable are window management state: they may only be made during a manage sequence and take effect after it.

request.name: destroy
request.description: A gesture in progress through this binding stays consumed until it ends, without further events.

request.name: disable
request.description: A gesture already in progress through this binding continues to be reported until it ends.

event.name: update
event.description: dx and dy are the summed motion of the fingers' centre since the previous update, in the same accelerated units as pointer motion (libinput reports no unaccelerated gesture deltas through wlroots). scale is the pinch scale relative to the begin (1 for swipe), rotation the summed rotation in degrees clockwise since the previous update (0 for swipe). Hold gestures have no updates.

event.name: end
event.description: cancelled is 1 if libinput cancelled the gesture (for example a finger was added or lifted early), 0 otherwise.

interface.name: newm_river_axis_binding_v1
interface.description: enable and disable are window management state: they may only be made during a manage sequence and take effect after it.

request.name: set_sources
request.description: Match only axis events from the given sources: events from other sources go on to the next matching binding, else to the client under the pointer. For example a binding of the wheel source only zooms with Super+wheel while Super+two-finger touchpad scrolling still reaches the application. The default is every source (version 1 behaviour); with none the binding matches nothing. This is window management state, like enable.

event.name: axis
event.description: The summed axis motion since the previous axis event: value in the units of wl_pointer.axis, value120 in the units of wl_pointer.axis_value120 (0 for continuous sources), and the source of the latest event.
